fields.meta_title: Job Application Form Template and Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Make a job application form that takes resumes and keeps every applicant in a table you own. Print a blank PDF for walk-ins. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Job Application Form That Feeds Your Hiring Pipeline
fields.hero_description: Describe the role and what each applicant must provide. Emergent builds the job application form and the applicant table behind it, in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Every Job Application Form Needs
fields.features_subheading: A job application form asks each candidate the same questions. Emergent adds role branching, uploads, PDFs and an applicant table.
fields.feature_1:
Every section, field by field

Emergent drafts the six standard sections with the right input for each answer: a date picker for the start date, a phone field and a block that repeats for each past employer.
fields.feature_2:
One form for every open role

Applicants pick a position and see only the questions written for it. A forklift operator is asked for a certification date; a bookkeeper names the accounting software they use.
fields.feature_3:
Resume and certificate uploads

Applicants attach a resume and any license or certificate the role needs from a phone, without creating an account. Each file is stored with the application it arrived on.
fields.feature_4:
A filled PDF of every application

Each online application can be kept as a filled PDF in the same layout for the personnel file, typed signature included. Name each file by applicant and role, like Haddad_RN.pdf.
fields.feature_5:
An applicant table with hiring stages

Every application lands as a row with role, location, stage and owner, in a table that never caps applications. The app then alerts the hiring manager by Slack or email.
fields.feature_6:
Your careers page, your source code

Publish the form on your own domain or embed it in the careers page you already run. Your developers get the full source in GitHub for anything the prompt did not cover.

fields.usecase_heading: Job Application Forms for Every Hire
fields.tab_content_1:
Know who can work weekends before you call

The first question is which store. Applicants then give a start date and tap the shifts they can work. That store's manager hears about it in Slack, and the applicant table filters by weekend availability.
fields.tab_content_2:
Catch any license due to lapse within 60 days

Each nurse gives a license number and the state that issued it, and medical assistants give their certification. Every expiry date has its own field, and the recruiter sees the flag before an interview is booked. BLS and ACLS cards upload on the same screen.
fields.tab_content_3:
Current managers hear about internal moves in private

Employees apply with their employee ID and their months in the current role. This posting asks for at least 12, and anyone short of it is told before they submit. Eligible applications reach the person's current manager as a Slack direct message and go to a table kept apart from outside candidates.
fields.tab_content_4:
The shortlist skips anyone who fails a must-have

Designers upload a resume and a portfolio, then say whether they are authorized to work in the US and what salary they expect. Anyone without work authorization, or asking above the posted band, goes to a hold list. The rest land in the design team's hiring channel in Slack as a shortlist.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Job Application Form
fields.howto_description: Settle what the role requires before you write a single question. Seven steps take you from that list to a published form that fills an applicant table.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down what the role requires
fields.howto_step_1_des: List what you need to know before a first call: availability, location, licenses, the right to work and expected pay. Drop any question that would not change the decision, and generally avoid ones that reveal age or religion. Several states also ban asking for pay history.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for two or three references, each with a phone number and how they know the applicant, and decide whether anyone calls them before or after an interview. The form closes with a statement the applicant signs and dates: I certify that my answers are true and complete.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Name each position in the prompt with the questions only it needs, and mark which are required. Keep each role's extras to a handful, since the shared sections carry most of the form. A long role-specific block usually belongs in a later screening step.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide which files each role requires. A resume can be optional for cashiers and required for office roles, while a cover letter stays optional everywhere. Limit uploads to PDF and DOCX files under 10 MB each.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose who hears about each application and how: the store manager in Slack, the recruiter by email. Then name the stages every applicant moves through before an offer. With a stage column added, the applicant table becomes the hiring pipeline your managers filter each morning.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide how paper applications get in. A QR code at the counter opens the same form on a phone. When someone hands in a paper copy instead, a manager types it in through the online form and it joins the table like any other.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Put the form on your careers page or your own domain, then submit a test application for every role. Check that each role shows its own questions and that the alert reaches the right person before the link goes out.

scope.evidence: H1 "Build a Job Application Form That Feeds Your Hiring Pipeline", meta title "Job Application Form Template and Builder | Emergent" and hero "Emergent builds the job application form and the applicant table behind it" state the whole job.

intent.evidence: The top 10 is blank PDFs and .doc files. The page gives the document's content field by field (FAQ 3 six sections, step 2 certification wording "I certify that my answers are true and complete"), a one-page version (FAQ 7) and a printable blank PDF (feature_4, FAQ 4), then what a PDF cannot do. Accepted P2: F5, no PAA box on this SERP, so the FAQ comes from related searches and secondaries.

specificity.evidence: Hiring vocabulary throughout: "A forklift operator is asked for a certification date", "Each nurse gives a license number and the state that issued it", "May we contact this employer?". The table uses the hiring variant ("Prompt for the application form and the hiring pipeline around it", "Resumes and portfolios saved to storage you own, no sign-in").

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens with a full sentence: "Emergent drafts the six standard sections", "Applicants pick a position", "The first question is which store.", "Employees apply with their employee ID", "Designers upload a resume and a portfolio" (rows 2 and 16 clear).

craft.evidence: No tacked-on endings (Q5 clean). Cycle-4 fixes hold: FAQ 6 no longer ends on an appended secondary, and the serial comma is absent page-wide (feature_1 "a phone field and a block", feature_5 "stage and owner", FAQ 3 "references and a signed, dated certification"). Restatement overlaps logged as notes and under faq.

voice.evidence: Reads like an operator: "Separate copies per role tend to drift: the cashier form gets a new availability question and the stock clerk form never does." Cycle-4 fixes hold: four outcome tab H3s in different shapes ("Know who can work weekends before you call", "The shortlist skips anyone who fails a must-have"), no run of "Yes." openers (FAQ 6 opens "They are the same document."), and the hero and subheading are specific.

truth.evidence: All 9 claims_used ids are approved. Domain claims are sourced (EEOC, DOL, OSHA 1910.178(l), 49 CFR 391.21, NCSBN, AAMA, AHA). Tab 4 rule now stated: "Anyone without work authorization, or asking above the posted band, goes to a hold list." Tab 2 H3 no longer overclaims. Why description no longer generalizes about competitors. Image numbers agree: 52 days under 60, 18 months against 12, shortlist 3 + hold 1.

distinct.evidence: Tab H3s no longer share creator-application's "[A] X application that Y" shape; plan-check 0 warnings. Payroll goes to new-employee-form (FAQ 8), scored screening to candidate-screening-form (FAQ 10), and tab 4 keeps to two yes/no must-haves.

findings.quote: Your form can produce a free, printable job application form PDF, blank and sized for letter paper, for people who apply in person. Every online application can be exported too, as a filled copy ending with the typed signature and date.
findings.issue: FAQ 4 restates feature_4 point for point: feature_4 says "Print the blank form for walk-ins at the front counter. Each application that arrives online can also be kept as a filled PDF in the same layout, ready for the personnel file." Same class: FAQ 1 "the copy for whoever gets hired goes into the personnel file" echoes feature_4 "ready for the personnel file", and howto_step_6_des "a few blank printed copies cover anyone without one" is a third telling of the blank-copy point (the meta description may mirror it).
findings.fix: Say each point once. Keep FAQ 4's answer-first yes and the letter-size blank PDF, then add something the body does not say, in place of the filled-copy sentence. Keep the filled copy in feature_4 only, and drop the personnel-file echo from one of FAQ 1 or feature_4.

findings.quote: a block that repeats for each past employer / Work history repeats for every past job the applicant lists / Emergent drafts the six standard sections / ask for the standard set / the first draft arrives with every standard section in place
findings.issue: The repeating work-history block and the standard-sections draft are each said two or three times.
findings.fix: Let feature_1 own the repeating block. Step 2 keeps the references and the certification, and FAQ 5 leads on pasting HR's own template.

findings.quote: A forklift operator is asked for a certification date; a bookkeeper names the accounting software they use. / A delivery role might ask about a driver's license and recent moving violations, while a cashier role skips both.
findings.issue: Two parallel two-role examples make the same point about role branching.
findings.fix: Keep one example pair, and give step 3 its own content (the handful-of-questions limit is already there).

findings.quote: never ask about age, religion or family plans
findings.issue: The cited EEOC page discourages age questions and says they draw scrutiny. It does not ban them, and standard applications lawfully ask whether the applicant meets a minimum age. "Never ask about age" goes beyond the source.
findings.fix: "never ask for a date of birth, religion or family plans; ask only whether the applicant meets the role's minimum age".

findings.quote: the copy for whoever gets hired goes into the personnel file
findings.issue: An unsourced record-keeping claim. Read alone, it implies only the hire's application is kept, while EEOC rules require employers to keep all applications for a period.
findings.fix: Cut the clause, or source and reword it ("every application is kept on file; the hire's copy joins the personnel file").

findings.quote: Each application that arrives online can also be kept as a filled PDF in the same layout
findings.issue: PDF generation has no ledger entry of its own and maps only to prompt-build.
findings.fix: Coordinator to confirm prompt-build covers generated PDFs, or add a ledger entry.

The certification statement says the applicant's answers are true and complete
Employers may ask whether an applicant is legally authorized to work in the US

Medical assistants are mostly unlicensed by states; the CMA is a certification awarded by the AAMA
BLS and ACLS are provider cards issued after American Heart Association courses
Internal transfer policies commonly set a minimum time in the current role and involve the current manager
Application questions that would reveal age or religion should generally be avoided
Employers may ask for expected pay; a number of states ban asking for pay history
Forklift operators are trained and certified by the employer under OSHA 1910.178(l)
Employers covered by EEOC rules keep all application forms, hired or not, for one year
